00001| /**
00002|  * OpenCode in-sandbox runner.
00003|  *
00004|  * This file is shipped INTO the sandbox by the orchestrator and executed there as
00005|  * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally
00006|  * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
00007|  * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
00008|  * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.
00009|  *
00010|  * Dual mode:
00011|  *   - runnable: invoked directly → reads argv, runs the agent, writes the result
00012|  *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.
00013|  *   - importable: `import { runAgent } from './run.mjs'` → returns a RunnerResult
00014|  *     (no file write, no exit). This is what a future in-sandbox judge reuses.
00015|  *
00016|  * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be
00017|  * unit-tested directly — the same code the sandbox runs (see opencode.test.ts).
00018|  */
00019| 
00020| import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
00021| import { mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';
00022| import { dirname } from 'node:path';
00023| import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
00024| 
00025| /**
00026|  * Build the OpenCode CLI argument list.
00027|  *
00028|  *   - `run <prompt> --format json` is always emitted (`--format json` gives the
00029|  *     structured JSON event stream we parse for the transcript).
00030|  *   - `--model <extra.cliModel>` is appended when a model override is present.
00031|  *     cliModel is HOST-computed (resolveOpenCodeModel in agent.ts, threaded via
00032|  *     runnerExtra like codex's resolved model) so a canonical gateway id like
00033|  *     `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` arrives as `vercel/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` —
00034|  *     the form OpenCode routes through the configured `vercel` provider. There is
00035|  *     deliberately NO fallback to input.model: passing it verbatim is the exact
00036|  *     mis-route this fixes, and both runner entry points (the orchestrator and
00037|  *     the judge's eval-helper) always ship extra.
00038|  *   - else, when modelPolicy === 'native-default', `--print-logs --log-level INFO`
00039|  *     is appended so older OpenCode versions print the CLI-selected model (the
00040|  *     log-scrape path) without a follow-up export call.
00041|  *
00042|  * @param {{prompt:string, modelPolicy?:string, extra?:Record<string,unknown>}} input
00043|  * @returns {string[]}
00044|  */
00045| export function buildOpenCodeCliArgs(input) {
00046|   const cliArgs = ['run', input.prompt, '--format', 'json'];
00047|   const cliModel = input.extra?.cliModel;
00048|   if (cliModel) {
00049|     cliArgs.push('--model', String(cliModel));
00050|   } else if (input.modelPolicy === 'native-default') {
00051|     cliArgs.push('--print-logs', '--log-level', 'INFO');
00052|   }
00053|   return cliArgs;
00054| }
00055| 
00056| /**
00057|  * Report the observed model in the caller's namespace.
00058|  *
00059|  * When the host prefixed the requested model with `vercel/` (extra.cliModel !==
00060|  * input.model), OpenCode observes it back in its own provider namespace —
00061|  * `vercel/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` for a requested `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`.
00062|  * Un-apply exactly that translation so observed === requested holds for callers
00063|  * that speak canonical gateway ids, and a gateway substitution still surfaces as
00064|  * a clean gateway id (`anthropic/claude-haiku-4`, not `vercel/anthropic/...`).
00065|  *
00066|  * Everything else passes through untouched: native-default runs (no override —
00067|  * consumers already treat `vercel/google/gemini-3-pro-preview` as canonical),
00068|  * callers that already speak OpenCode's namespace (`vercel/...` requested), and
00069|  * extraProviders runs (their providerID isn't `vercel`).
00070|  *
00071|  * @param {string|undefined} observedModel
00072|  * @param {{model?:string, extra?:Record<string,unknown>}} input
00073|  * @returns {string|undefined}
00074|  */
00075| export function normalizeObservedModel(observedModel, input) {
00076|   if (!observedModel) {
00077|     return observedModel;
00078|   }
00079|   const cliModel = input.extra?.cliModel;
00080|   const hostPrefixed = typeof cliModel === 'string' && cliModel !== input.model;
00081|   if (hostPrefixed && observedModel.startsWith('vercel/')) {
00082|     return observedModel.slice('vercel/'.length);
00083|   }
00084|   return observedModel;
00085| }
00086| 
00087| /**
00088|  * Extract transcript from OpenCode JSON output.
00089|  * When run with --format json, OpenCode outputs JSON events to stdout.
00090|  * Preserved verbatim from the old adapter.
00091|  *
00092|  * @param {string|undefined|null} output
00093|  * @returns {string|undefined}
00094|  */
00095| export function extractTranscriptFromOutput(output) {
00096|   if (!output || !output.trim()) {
00097|     return undefined;
00098|   }
00099| 
00100|   // The --format json output contains JSON events, one per line.
00101|   // Filter to only include lines that look like JSON objects.
00102|   const lines = output.split('\n').filter((line) => {
00103|     const trimmed = line.trim();
00104|     return trimmed.startsWith('{') && trimmed.endsWith('}');
00105|   });
00106| 
00107|   if (lines.length === 0) {
00108|     return undefined;
00109|   }
00110| 
00111|   return lines.join('\n');
00112| }
00113| 
00114| /**
00115|  * Scrape the OpenCode printed logs for the primary build model.
00116|  * Works on OpenCode <= 1.16.x, whose INFO log lines carry providerID/modelID.
00117|  * Preserved verbatim from the old adapter.
00118|  *
00119|  * @param {string} output
00120|  * @returns {string|undefined}
00121|  */
00122| export function extractObservedModelFromOpenCodeOutput(output) {
00123|   let observedModel;
00124| 
00125|   for (const line of output.split('\n')) {
00126|     if (!line.includes('service=llm') || !line.includes('small=false') || !line.includes('agent=build')) {
00127|       continue;
00128|     }
00129| 
00130|     const providerMatch = line.match(/providerID=([^\s]+)/);
00131|     const modelMatch = line.match(/modelID=([^\s]+)/);
00132|     const providerID = providerMatch?.[1];
00133|     const modelID = modelMatch?.[1];
00134|     if (providerID && modelID) {
00135|       observedModel = `${providerID}/${modelID}`;
00136|     }
00137|   }
00138| 
00139|   return observedModel;
00140| }
00141| 
00142| /**
00143|  * Extract the session id from the `--format json` event stream.
00144|  * Every emitted event carries a `sessionID` field.
00145|  * Preserved verbatim from the old adapter.
00146|  *
00147|  * @param {string|undefined} transcript
00148|  * @returns {string|undefined}
00149|  */
00150| export function extractSessionIdFromTranscript(transcript) {
00151|   if (!transcript) {
00152|     return undefined;
00153|   }
00154| 
00155|   for (const line of transcript.split('\n')) {
00156|     try {
00157|       const event = JSON.parse(line);
00158|       if (typeof event.sessionID === 'string' && event.sessionID) {
00159|         return event.sessionID;
00160|       }
00161|     } catch {
00162|       // Skip non-JSON lines

/**
 * OpenCode in-sandbox runner.
 *
 * This file is shipped INTO the sandbox by the orchestrator and executed there as
 * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally
 * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
 * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
 * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.
 *
 * Dual mode:
 *   - runnable: invoked directly → reads argv, runs the agent, writes the result
 *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.
 *   - importable: `import { runAgent } from './run.mjs'` → returns a RunnerResult
 *     (no file write, no exit). This is what a future in-sandbox judge reuses.
 *
 * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be
 * unit-tested directly — the same code the sandbox runs (see opencode.test.ts).
 */

import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

00024| 
00025| /**
00026|  * Build the OpenCode CLI argument list.
00027|  *
00028|  *   - `run <prompt> --format json` is always emitted (`--format json` gives the
00029|  *     structured JSON event stream we parse for the transcript).
00030|  *   - `--model <extra.cliModel>` is appended when a model override is present.
00031|  *     cliModel is HOST-computed (resolveOpenCodeModel in agent.ts, threaded via
00032|  *     runnerExtra like codex's resolved model) so a canonical gateway id like
00033|  *     `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` arrives as `vercel/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` —
00034|  *     the form OpenCode routes through the configured `vercel` provider. There is
00035|  *     deliberately NO fallback to input.model: passing it verbatim is the exact
00036|  *     mis-route this fixes, and both runner entry points (the orchestrator and
00037|  *     the judge's eval-helper) always ship extra.
00038|  *   - else, when modelPolicy === 'native-default', `--print-logs --log-level INFO`
00039|  *     is appended so older OpenCode versions print the CLI-selected model (the
00040|  *     log-scrape path) without a follow-up export call.

00043|  * @returns {string[]}

00046|   const cliArgs = ['run', input.prompt, '--format', 'json'];
00047|   const cliModel = input.extra?.cliModel;
00048|   if (cliModel) {
00049|     cliArgs.push('--model', String(cliModel));
00050|   } else if (input.modelPolicy === 'native-default') {
00051|     cliArgs.push('--print-logs', '--log-level', 'INFO');
00052|   }
00053|   return cliArgs;
00054| }

00056| /**

00058|  *

00060|  * input.model), OpenCode observes it back in its own provider namespace —
00061|  * `vercel/anthropic/claude-sonnet-5` for a requested `anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`.
00062|  * Un-apply exactly that translation so observed === requested holds for callers
00063|  * that speak canonical gateway ids, and a gateway substitution still surfaces as
00064|  * a clean gateway id (`anthropic/claude-haiku-4`, not `vercel/anthropic/...`).

00067|  * consumers already treat `vercel/google/gemini-3-pro-preview` as canonical),
00068|  * callers that already speak OpenCode's namespace (`vercel/...` requested), and
00069|  * extraProviders runs (their providerID isn't `vercel`).

00073|  * @returns {string|undefined}
00074|  */
00075| export function normalizeObservedModel(observedModel, input) {
00076|   if (!observedModel) {
00077|     return observedModel;
00078|   }
00079|   const cliModel = input.extra?.cliModel;
00080|   const hostPrefixed = typeof cliModel === 'string' && cliModel !== input.model;
00081|   if (hostPrefixed && observedModel.startsWith('vercel/')) {
00082|     return observedModel.slice('vercel/'.length);

00084|   return observedModel;
00085| }
00086| 
00087| /**
00088|  * Extract transcript from OpenCode JSON output.
00089|  * When run with --format json, OpenCode outputs JSON events to stdout.
00090|  * Preserved verbatim from the old adapter.
00091|  *
00092|  * @param {string|undefined|null} output
00093|  * @returns {string|undefined}
00094|  */
00095| export function extractTranscriptFromOutput(output) {
00096|   if (!output || !output.trim()) {
00097|     return undefined;
00098|   }
00099| 
00100|   // The --format json output contains JSON events, one per line.
00101|   // Filter to only include lines that look like JSON objects.
00102|   const lines = output.split('\n').filter((line) => {
00103|     const trimmed = line.trim();

00105|   });

00107|   if (lines.length === 0) {

00109|   }

00111|   return lines.join('\n');

00114| /**
00115|  * Scrape the OpenCode printed logs for the primary build model.
00116|  * Works on OpenCode <= 1.16.x, whose INFO log lines carry providerID/modelID.
00117|  * Preserved verbatim from the old adapter.
00118|  *
00119|  * @param {string} output
00120|  * @returns {string|undefined}
00121|  */
00122| export function extractObservedModelFromOpenCodeOutput(output) {
00123|   let observedModel;
00124| 
00125|   for (const line of output.split('\n')) {
00126|     if (!line.includes('service=llm') || !line.includes('small=false') || !line.includes('agent=build')) {
00127|       continue;
00128|     }
00129| 
00130|     const providerMatch = line.match(/providerID=([^\s]+)/);

00132|     const providerID = providerMatch?.[1];
00133|     const modelID = modelMatch?.[1];
00134|     if (providerID && modelID) {

00136|     }
00137|   }
00138| 
00139|   return observedModel;
00140| }

00142| /**
00143|  * Extract the session id from the `--format json` event stream.
00144|  * Every emitted event carries a `sessionID` field.
00145|  * Preserved verbatim from the old adapter.
00146|  *
00147|  * @param {string|undefined} transcript
00148|  * @returns {string|undefined}
00149|  */

00153|   }

00155|   for (const line of transcript.split('\n')) {

00169| /**

00171|  * Assistant messages carry `providerID` and `modelID` in their info.

00174|  * @param {string} exportOutput
00175|  * @returns {string|undefined}
00176|  */

00184|   try {

00188|   }

00190|   const messages = parsed.messages;

00192|     return undefined;
00193|   }

00195|   for (const message of messages) {

00197|     if (info?.role !== 'assistant') {
00198|       continue;

00211| /**
00212|  * Run OpenCode over the workspace at `input.cwd` and return a RunnerResult.
00213|  *
00214|  * Auth (AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, and OPENCODE_ENABLE_EXA when web research is on)
00215|  * arrives via process.env — the orchestrator sets it on the `node run.mjs`
00216|  * invocation, and we pass process.env straight through to the CLI. The runner
00217|  * never handles secrets itself.
00218|  *
00219|  * @param {import('../plugin/contract.js').AgentRunInput} input
00220|  * @returns {Promise<import('../plugin/contract.js').RunnerResult>}
00221|  */
00222| export async function runAgent(input) {
00223|   const args = buildOpenCodeCliArgs(input);
00224| 
00225|   // spawnSync (not a shell string): the prompt is a plain argv element, so there
00226|   // is no shell quoting/escaping to get wrong. Blocking is fine — the runner has
00227|   // nothing else to do while the agent works. The sandbox-level timeout bounds it.
00228|   const res = spawnSync('opencode', args, {
00229|     cwd: input.cwd,
00230|     env: process.env,
00231|     encoding: 'utf8',
00232|     maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024,
00233|   });

00235|   const stdout = res.stdout || '';
00236|   const stderr = res.stderr || '';

00242|   // Capture the transcript from the combined output (old: over stdout+stderr).
00243|   const transcript = extractTranscriptFromOutput(output) ?? null;

00246|   // include it, so first try scraping the printed logs (works on OpenCode <=
00247|   // 1.16.x), then fall back to `opencode export <sessionID>`, whose assistant
00248|   // messages carry providerID/modelID (OpenCode 1.17.0 changed the log format,
00249|   // which broke the scrape). Observation must never fail the run.

00252|     const sessionId = extractSessionIdFromTranscript(transcript ?? undefined);

00254|       try {
00255|         const exportRes = spawnSync('opencode', ['export', sessionId], {
00256|           cwd: input.cwd,
00257|           env: process.env,
00258|           encoding: 'utf8',
00259|           maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024,
00260|         });

00262|           observedModel = extractObservedModelFromSessionExport(exportRes.stdout || '');
00263|         }
00264|       } catch {
00265|         // Leave observedModel undefined.
00266|       }
00267|     }
00268|   }
00269|   const observedModelOrNull = normalizeObservedModel(observedModel, input) ?? null;

00271|   if (res.error || agentExitCode !== 0) {
00272|     // Mirror the old error string: last 5 lines of output, else a coded fallback.
00273|     const errorLines = output.trim().split('\n').slice(-5).join('\n');
00274|     const fallback = res.error
00275|       ? `Failed to run opencode: ${res.error.message}`
00276|       : `OpenCode CLI exited with code ${agentExitCode}`;

00278|       ok: false,
00279|       output,
00280|       transcript,
00281|       observedModel: observedModelOrNull,
00282|       error: errorLines || fallback,
00283|       agentExitCode,
00284|     };
00285|   }
00286| 
00287|   return {
00288|     ok: true,
00289|     output,
00290|     transcript,
00291|     observedModel: observedModelOrNull,
00292|     error: null,
00293|     agentExitCode,
00294|   };
00295| }
00296| 
00297| /* ─────────────────────────── runnable (CLI) entry ─────────────────────────── */
00298| 
00299| // True when this file is executed directly (`node run.mjs ...`), false when imported.
00300| const isMain = process.argv[1] && fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) === process.argv[1];
00301| 
00302| if (isMain) {

00304|   const input = JSON.parse(process.argv[2]);

00306|   // Always produce a RunnerResult, even if the runner itself throws, so the host
00307|   // always has a result file to read (node exit code stays 0 except on a truly
00308|   // unrecoverable crash before we can write).
00309|   let result;
00310|   try {
00311|     result = await runAgent(input);
00312|   } catch (e) {
00313|     result = {
00314|       ok: false,
00315|       output: '',
00316|       transcript: null,
00317|       observedModel: null,
00318|       error: e && e.message ? e.message : String(e),
00319|       agentExitCode: -1,
00320|     };
00321|   }

00323|   // Source of truth: the result file the host reads back via sandbox.readFile.
00324|   try {
00325|     mkdirSync(dirname(input.resultPath), { recursive: true });

00329|   }
00330| 
00331|   // Fallback channel: a compact status line (no transcript — it can be huge).
00332|   process.stdout.write(
00333|     '__AGENT_RESULT__ ' +
00334|       JSON.stringify({
00335|         ok: result.ok,
00336|         observedModel: result.observedModel,
00337|         error: result.error,
00338|         agentExitCode: result.agentExitCode,
00339|       }) +
00340|       '\n'
00341|   );

00343|   // Exit 0: "the runner ran". Agent success/failure is conveyed via result.ok, not
00344|   // the node exit code (the host distinguishes the two).
00345|   process.exit(0);
00346| }

 * This file is shipped INTO the sandbox by the orchestrator and executed there as

title: updateTag
description: API Reference for the updateTag function.
---

`updateTag` allows you to update cached data on-demand for a specific cache tag from within [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data).

This function is designed for **read-your-own-writes** scenarios, where a user makes a change (like creating a post), and the UI immediately shows the change, rather than stale data.

## Usage

`updateTag` can **only** be called from within [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data). It cannot be used in Route Handlers, Client Components, or any other context.

If you need to invalidate cache tags in Route Handlers or other contexts, use [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) instead.

> **Good to know**: `updateTag` immediately expires the cached data for the specified tag. The next request will wait to fetch fresh data rather than serving stale content from the cache, ensuring users see their changes immediately.

---
title: updateTag
description: API Reference for the updateTag function.
---

`updateTag` allows you to update cached data on-demand for a specific cache tag from within [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data).

This function is designed for **read-your-own-writes** scenarios, where a user makes a change (like creating a post), and the UI immediately shows the change, rather than stale data.

## Usage

`updateTag` can **only** be called from within [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data). It cannot be used in Route Handlers, Client Components, or any other context.

If you need to invalidate cache tags in Route Handlers or other contexts, use [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) instead.

> **Good to know**: `updateTag` immediately expires the cached data for the specified tag. The next request will wait to fetch fresh data rather than serving stale content from the cache, ensuring users see their changes immediately.

## Parameters

```tsx

00062|     data: {
00063|       title: String(formData.get('title')),
00064|       authorId: session.user.id,
00065|     },
00066|   })
00067| 
00068|   revalidatePath('/posts')
00069| }
00070| ```
00071| 
00072| The mutation, the cache invalidation, and the page re-render all complete in a single roundtrip. Because [`redirect`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect#behavior) throws a control-flow exception, any code after it does not run. Place revalidation calls before `redirect` if the destination needs the fresh data.
00073| 
00074| [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) with a stale-while-revalidate profile is the exception: it marks the tag for background refresh and does **not** include a re-render in the action response. The page reflects the change on a later read. An action that does none of the above carries only its return value, and the current route is not re-rendered.
00075| 
00076| ## Security
00077| 
00078| A Server Action runs as a POST request against the page that invokes it. At build time, the `'use server'` directive tells the compiler to swap the function's implementation in client bundles for a reference (an action ID plus a dispatcher) that POSTs back to the server. The implementation stays on the server, but the route is reachable to anyone who can send the same POST. Treat every action as an untrusted entry point.
00079| 
00080| Next.js enforces a few framework-level protections:
00081| 
00082| - **CSRF check.** The request's `Origin` is compared to the `Host` (or `X-Forwarded-Host`). Mismatches are rejected. Configure [`serverActions.allowedOrigins`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/serverActions#allowedorigins) for proxy or CDN domains.
00083| - **Body size limit.** Action requests are capped at 1MB by default. Configure [`serverActions.bodySizeLimit`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/serverActions#bodysizelimit) when accepting larger payloads.
00084| - **Encrypted action IDs and dead code elimination.** Action references are encrypted at build time, and unused Server Functions are stripped from client bundles so they have no public endpoint. See [Built-in Server Actions security features](/docs/app/guides/data-security#built-in-server-actions-security-features).
00085| - **Closure variable encryption.** Variables captured by an inline action are encrypted before being sent to the client. For multi-instance and self-hosted deployments, set `NEXT_SERVER_ACTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` to a stable key shared across instances. See [Closures and encryption](/docs/app/guides/data-security#closures-and-encryption).
00086| 
00087| Framework protections are not a substitute for application-level checks. Inside every action:
00088| 
00089| - **Authenticate and authorize.** Render-time gating (only rendering a form on an authenticated page) is not a security boundary, because requests can be sent without going through the UI.
00090| - **Validate inputs.** Treat `FormData`, query parameters, and headers as untrusted.
00091| - **Constrain return values.** Action returns are serialized to the client. Shape them to what the UI renders, not raw database records.
00092| 
00093| For end-to-end patterns including a Data Access Layer, return-value tainting, and rate limiting, see the [Data Security guide](/docs/app/guides/data-security#mutating-data).
00094| 
00095| Destructive operations like deletes may warrant stronger handling, such as elevated session checks or re-authentication, and a loud failure when those checks miss.
00096| 
00097| ```ts filename="app/posts/actions.ts" highlight={6,7,8}
00098| 'use server'
00099| 
00100| import { auth } from '@/lib/auth'
00101| 
00102| export async function deletePost(postId: string) {
00103|   const session = await auth()
00104|   if (!session?.user) throw new Error('Unauthorized')
00105|   if (!(await canDelete(session.user, postId))) throw new Error('Forbidden')
00106| 
00107|   await db.post.delete({ where: { id: postId } })
00108| }
00109| ```
00110| 
00111| If you've enabled the experimental [`authInterrupts`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/authInterrupts) flag, you can throw [`unauthorized()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unauthorized) and [`forbidden()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/forbidden) from `next/navigation` instead, so Next.js renders the corresponding `unauthorized.tsx` / `forbidden.tsx` UI segment automatically.
00112| 
00113| For example, a client legitimately tells the server _which_ item to act on, but it should not supply the row's contents or ownership. Send a reference (typically an ID) plus the user's change, and re-read the rest from a trusted source using the session. Schema validation (zod or similar) only checks the _shape_ of the input. A well-formed `Item` object can still refer to a row the caller does not own.
00114| 
00115| ```ts filename="app/items/actions.ts"

00117| 
00118| import { auth } from '@/lib/auth'
00119| import { db } from '@/lib/db'

00122| // from the client, so anyone who can POST here can mark any item complete.

00124|   await db.item.update({ where: { id: item.id }, data: { completed: true } })
00125| }
00126|

00128| export async function completeItem(itemId: string) {
00129|   const session = await auth()
00130|   if (!session?.user) return
00131| 
00132|   const item = await db.item.findFirst({
00133|     where: { id: itemId, ownerId: session.user.id },
00134|   })
00135|   if (!item) return
00136| 
00137|   await db.item.update({ where: { id: item.id }, data: { completed: true } })
00138| }

For multi-instance and self-hosted deployments, set `NEXT_SERVER_ACTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` to a stable key shared across instances. 00087| Framework protections are not a substitute for application-level checks. Inside every action:

00089| - **Authenticate and authorize.** Render-time gating (only rendering a form on an authenticated page) is not a security boundary, because requests can be sent without going through the UI.

00099| 
00100| import { auth } from '@/lib/auth'
00101| 
00102| export async function deletePost(postId: string) {
00103|   const session = await auth()
00104|   if (!session?.user) throw new Error('Unauthorized')
00105|   if (!(await canDelete(session.user, postId))) throw new Error('Forbidden')

00107|   await db.post.delete({ where: { id: postId } })
00108| }

00021| 
00022| You create one by adding the [`'use server'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-server) directive, then invoke it from a form, or from an event handler or `useEffect` wrapped in `startTransition`. For the basics of creating and invoking Server Functions, see [Mutating data](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) and the [Forms guide](/docs/app/guides/forms).
00023| 
00024| This page covers the parts of Server Actions that are specific to Next.js: how they commonly map to mutations, how the response carries both returned data and re-rendered UI, how the client dispatches them, the security boundary the framework enforces, and the configuration available.
00025| 
00026| ## Sequential dispatch on the client
00027| 
00028| Next.js dispatches Server Actions one at a time per client. If a user triggers three actions in quick succession, the second waits for the first to finish, then the third waits for the second. This keeps the re-rendered server tree consistent with the action result that produced it.

metadata.preview:
You create one by adding the [`'use server'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-server) directive, then invoke it from a form, or from an event handler or `useEffect` wrapped in `startTransition`. For the basics of creating and invoking Server Functions, see [Mutating data](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) and the [Forms guide](/docs/app/guides/forms).

This page covers the parts of Server Actions that are specific to Next.js: how they commonly map to mutations, how the response carries both returned data and re-rendered UI, how the client dispatches them, the security boundary the framework enforces, and the configuration available.

## Sequential dispatch on the client

Next.js dispatches Server Actions one at a time per client. If a user triggers three actions in quick succession, the second waits for the first to finish, then the third waits for the second. This keeps the re-rendered server tree consistent with the action result that produced it.

A consequence: do not rely on `Promise.all` to parallelize Server Actions from the client. If you need parallel work, do it inside a single Server Action, fetch in parallel from a [Server Component](/docs/app/getting-started/fetching-data#server-components), or use a [Route Handler](/docs/app/guides/backend-for-frontend#manipulating-data) for non-mutation requests.

> **Good to know:** This is a property of the client dispatcher, not of Server Functions in general. Server-side, an action runs in its own request and can do anything an async function can do.

## A single response carries data and UI

When a Server Action triggers an immediate revalidation, Next.js does the work inside one HTTP request: it runs the action, then re-renders the current route server-side. The response that comes back contains both pieces in the same Flight stream:

- The action's return value, consumed by `useActionState` or the awaited promise on the client.
- A newly rendered [RSC Payload](/docs/app/glossary#rsc-payload) for the current route, which the client commits as a seeded navigation.

events.content:
The admin product catalog page has been implemented in `app/page.tsx` with:

- Catalog caching using `unstable_cache` wrapping `getAllProducts` from `lib/db.js` tagged with `"products"`.
- An inline Server Action (`syncCatalog`) within the page component triggering stale-while-revalidate invalidation via `revalidateTag('products', 'max')`.
- A regular HTML `<form action={syncCatalog}>` featuring a "Sync latest catalog" submit button allowing admins to continue browsing without blocking on fresh recomputations.

The admin product catalog page has been implemented in `app/page.tsx` with:

- Catalog caching using `unstable_cache` wrapping `getAllProducts` from `lib/db.js` tagged with `"products"`.
- An inline Server Action (`syncCatalog`) within the page component triggering stale-while-revalidate invalidation via `revalidateTag('products', 'max')`.
- A regular HTML `<form action={syncCatalog}>` featuring a "Sync latest catalog" submit button allowing admins to continue browsing without blocking on fresh recomputations.
